A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same axiomatic interpretation framework and retain the same 2-SAT study despite the changed title. The complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Transformer training results, including 99.76% 2-SAT test accuracy, attention and neuron analyses, and empirical validation of mechanistic interpretations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds its own modular-addition interpretation validation and synthetic-error experiments. These new evaluations are distinct from the underlying models and interpretations attributed to prior work.

M1.justification: The 2-SAT model and interpretation procedure are retained, but the validation method is substantially extended. Appendix B.1 introduces graph-based interventions, a parallel-intervention formulation, and circuit linearization. Section 5 and Appendix H add an adaptation for continuous intermediate representations using discretization, downstream-equivalence classes, and learned linear abstraction/concretization maps.

E1.justification: V1 empirically studies only 2-SAT; v2 also evaluates the interpretation of a Transformer performing addition modulo 113. This adds a distinct task beyond Boolean satisfiability. The original 2-SAT coverage is retained. Appendix I explicitly leaves IOI unevaluated, so it does not constitute added empirical task coverage.

E2.justification: The decision-tree and disjunction-only interpretations remain the compared alternatives in the 2-SAT study. Nanda et al.'s model becomes an additional object of validation, not a competing baseline. The expanded discussions of causal abstraction and causal scrubbing do not add an empirical baseline comparison.

E3.justification: The original 2-SAT training and evaluation settings remain unchanged. New protocols include independently replacing each parsed clause with a random clause with 1% probability and evaluating propagation through all three components (Appendix F). Modular-addition evaluation introduces learned mappings using the original train/test split and tests rounding and downstream-equivalence discretizations (Section 5, Appendix H).

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a controlled error-injection analysis testing whether componentwise checks miss propagated interpretation errors. Section 5 and Appendix H add discretization sensitivity analyses showing that apparent internal agreement depends strongly on the equivalence criterion. The earlier attention analyses, decision-tree-size comparisons, and activation-amplification analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report epsilon using upper bounds from one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals. V2 clarifies that error estimation counts equality violations, but does not report a different uncertainty estimator, confidence level, repeated-run count, or seed-reporting scheme.

E6.justification: The original 2-SAT accuracy, axiom-error values, and neuron interpretation tables are retained. V2 adds modular-addition validation with epsilon 0.000335 under the selected discretization, versus epsilon 1 for second-component equivalence with one-decimal rounding. Its new Table 1 reports final-component prefix-equivalence error 0.0315 under injected noise versus 0.0128 without noise. These are new conditional results, not improvements to the original model.

T1.justification: Beyond the retained original axioms, v2 adds graph formulations and Axioms 7–11, a circuit-linearization construction, and an extensional-equivalence argument concerning restrictions on abstraction/concretization (Appendices B–C). Appendix E derives depth-dependent equivalence bounds and a replaceability bound under invertibility assumptions. Section 3 also explicitly requires discrete values for its equality tests.

C1.justification: V2 broadens the contribution from an axioms-guided 2-SAT interpretation to a framework for validating both existing and newly derived interpretations. Its claimed applicability also expands to circuit/subgraph analyses, which v1 explicitly excludes in its related work and limitations. The underlying claim that the 2-SAT model parses clauses and enumerates assignments remains unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive qualifications about discretization weakening internal-fidelity checks, unrestricted abstraction/concretization hiding computation, and redundant circuit computations masking interventions. It explains why IOI is not fully evaluated and why worst-case compositional bounds can be misleading. V1's blanket circuit exclusion is revised, while its explicit warning that the 2-SAT interpretation techniques require human effort and cannot be applied automatically is omitted.

D1.justification: V2 supplements the existing 2-SAT implementation descriptions with abstraction/concretization pseudocode in Listings 1–4. Appendix H and Listings 8–9 document modular-addition decomposition, mapping fitting, and the equivalence test. The implementation pointer changes from sat-mi to axiomatic-validation. The original 2-SAT hardware, data-generation instructions, and training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands its positioning against causal abstraction and causal scrubbing, discussing their mappings, interventions, and treatment of internal representations. It adds works including Chan et al. on causal scrubbing, Scheurer et al. on its pitfalls, and additional Geiger papers. Appendix C develops this comparison through an extensional-equivalence example, beyond v1's brief related-work discussion.

P1.justification: The title and narrative are reframed around validation. Existing data/model and interpretation sections are consolidated into a 2-SAT case study, previously separated axiom checks are grouped together, and probing/attention related work moves to Appendix A. Terminology is systematically refined from layers to Transformer blocks and from embeddings to representations, alongside expanded explanations and appendix reorganization.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main-text layout and substantially rearranges existing displays, including moving v1 Figures 2–3 into the appendix. It adds an error-comparison table and diagrams for extensional equivalence, the 2-SAT decomposition, and IOI circuits. Existing plots are reformatted, while the two original neuron tables are retained as Tables 2–3.

improvement.justification: V1 supports its framework chiefly through intuitive motivation and one 2-SAT study. V2 substantially strengthens the central justification with compositional-error derivations, a controlled experiment showing what componentwise checks miss, and validation on an independently developed modular-addition interpretation. It also makes important applicability limits explicit. Modular-addition success depends on a discretization that weakens internal-fidelity checks, and IOI remains only a sketch; nevertheless, the stronger theoretical and empirical support provides a substantial net improvement.
